name: frequency-tree
title: Frequency tree
tagline: Frequency tree: a count inside an ellipse node at each junction (root total → stage counts), category words on the branches; a missing count derives, any node occludes to "?".
description: A two-stage frequency tree — the GCSE / Edexcel exam figure. An ellipse node holds a whole-number count at every junction: a root node (the total) fans into stage-1 nodes (each a category count), and each of those fans into stage-2 leaf nodes. The category words (Pass/Fail, Male/Female, Tea/Coffee, …) label the BRANCHES between the nodes, not the nodes themselves, and optional stage headers band the top (e.g. "Literacy", "Numeracy"). You write only the scenario — the branch words and the counts you know — and everything else is computed: every node position and branch line, a single missing sibling count (parent − the other siblings), a missing parent (the sum of its children), and the root total (the sum of the stage-1 counts). Nodes occlude to "?" independently (the "complete the frequency tree" question) or blank to an empty ellipse (a staged build or a whole-tree answer space), and highlight to trace an answer. Distinct from probability/tree, which draws probabilities ON the branches with an end-outcome column; this model draws counts inside the node bubbles.
whenToUse: Reach for this for the GCSE "frequency tree" topic: two categorical stages (a first split, then a second split within each) recorded as whole-number counts, drawn the exam way — counts inside oval nodes, the category words on the branches. Author the tree as the scenario: nodes is the first category (each entry a { label, count } where label is the branch word), and each node's children is the second category. Put the count you know inside each node; leave the single missing sibling in a group without a count and it is filled as the parent − the others (and the root total auto-sums from the stage-1 counts, or set root.count). Common configurations: complete the frequency tree — occlude the nodes the pupil must find (root, a stage-1 count, some leaves), give the rest, and the derivation stays correct behind the "?"; blank answer space — showCounts:false blanks every node (label the branches, keep the structure) for pupils to fill in; worked example — give enough counts and the rest derive and show; find a specific frequency — highlight the node that answers "how many passed both?" and occlude it, or highlight the path. Stage headers: pass stages:[{label:"Literacy"},{label:"Numeracy"}] to band the top like the exam. Cross-block convention in a lesson: keep the same categories on the same branches and the same structure across blocks — change only what is given, occluded or highlighted. A staged build reads well: open on the given nodes, then reveal one derived count per stage (parent − siblings up the tree). Take the pupil's completion values with gaps below the figure (this v1 is a stimulus; answering ON the nodes is a flagged future response mode). Synonyms a teacher might use: frequency tree, complete the frequency tree, two-way frequency, tree of counts, conditional frequencies, Venn/tree crossover. For probabilities on the branches and P(outcome) products, use probability/tree instead; for a grid of the same counts with row/column totals, statistics/two-way-table.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

stages.description: Optional bold column headers banding the top, one per branch stage — stages[0] labels the root→stage-1 branches, stages[1] the stage-1→stage-2 branches (e.g. [{label:"Literacy"},{label:"Numeracy"}]). Omit for no headers.

showCounts.description: Show the count inside every node. false renders every node as an EMPTY ellipse — the whole-tree answer space for "complete the frequency tree" (the branches stay labelled). Per-node occlude ("?") or blank does the same one node at a time. Default true.

root.description: The root node at the left — the total. Its count auto-sums from the stage-1 counts, so set it only to state the total explicitly or when the stage-1 counts are incomplete.

count.description: The total inside the root node. Omit to auto-sum from the stage-1 counts. Set occlude to pose it as "?".

occlude.description: Render the total as "?" (find-the-total). The count stays derived for the answer. Default false.

blank.description: Render the root as an empty ellipse (staged build / answer space). Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the root node. Default false.

items.description: A stage-1 node fanning from the root (the first category), optionally fanning into stage-2 children (the second category).

label.description: The category word on the BRANCH from the root into this node — e.g. "Male", "Female", "Right-handed". Drawn on the branch, not inside the node. Omit for an unlabelled branch.

count.description: The whole-number count INSIDE this node. OMIT to DERIVE it as the root total − the other stage-1 nodes when it is the only one missing. Set occlude to show it as "?" instead.

occlude.description: Render this node's count as "?" — the complete-the-tree hook. The ellipse stays visible; the count is still derived for the answer. Default false.

blank.description: Render an EMPTY ellipse (staged build / blank answer space). blank wins over occlude. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this node — ellipse, fill and count — to mark an answer. Default false.

items.description: A stage-2 node (the second category). May optionally fan into a third stage of children; omit children for the standard two-stage tree.

label.description: The category word on the BRANCH leading into this node — e.g. "Pass", "Fail", "Tea", "Coffee". Drawn on the branch between the parent node and this one, NOT inside the node. Omit for an unlabelled branch.

count.description: The whole-number count INSIDE this node. OMIT to DERIVE it: when exactly one node in a sibling group has no count it is filled as parent count − the other siblings. Set occlude to show it as "?" (the find-the-count question) instead of the derived value.

occlude.description: Render this node's count as "?" — the question hook ("complete the frequency tree"). The ellipse stays visible. The count is still derived for the answer/aria; only the display is hidden. Default false.

blank.description: Render an EMPTY ellipse (no count, no "?") — a staged build filling nodes one at a time, or the exam-style blank answer space. Different from occlude: "?" poses a question, blank poses nothing yet. If both are set, blank wins. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this node — its ellipse, fill and count — to trace or mark an answer. Default false.

items.description: A leaf node with no children of its own — the end of a path. Same shape as any node; this is as deep as the tree goes.

label.description: The category word on the BRANCH leading into this node — e.g. "Pass", "Fail", "Tea", "Coffee". Drawn on the branch between the parent node and this one, NOT inside the node. Omit for an unlabelled branch.

count.description: The whole-number count INSIDE this node. OMIT to DERIVE it: when exactly one node in a sibling group has no count it is filled as parent count − the other siblings. Set occlude to show it as "?" (the find-the-count question) instead of the derived value.

occlude.description: Render this node's count as "?" — the question hook ("complete the frequency tree"). The ellipse stays visible. The count is still derived for the answer/aria; only the display is hidden. Default false.

blank.description: Render an EMPTY ellipse (no count, no "?") — a staged build filling nodes one at a time, or the exam-style blank answer space. Different from occlude: "?" poses a question, blank poses nothing yet. If both are set, blank wins. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this node — its ellipse, fill and count — to trace or mark an answer. Default false.

children.description: An optional THIRD stage fanning from this node. Omit for a two-stage tree. Up to 4 nodes.
The stage-2 nodes fanning from this node (the second category). Omit for a one-stage tree. Up to 4 nodes.

nodes.description: The stage-1 nodes fanning from the root (the first category), top to bottom. Each carries a branch label and a count, and fans into stage-2 children. Up to 4. Every node position and branch line is derived from this structure — nothing is placed in pixels.

examples.label: Worked example — 60 members, gym use then class booking (all counts shown)
Complete the frequency tree — total and one leaf given, the rest to find
Blank answer space — structure and branch words only, every node empty
Find a frequency — how many walk AND are late? (answer highlighted, occluded)
Total auto-summed — root count omitted, derived from the stage-1 nodes
Hard case — long labels, root occluded, a whole side to derive
